Chief_Complaint.content: Patient presents with 'weird symptoms' for approximately 1.5–2 months.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Episodes have increased in frequency from initially weekly to now a couple of times per day.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Each episode lasts a few days.

During episodes the patient has difficulty holding a cup and finds it harder to drink.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient reports general fatigue and weakness.
Duration of recurrent episodes is approximately 1.5–2 months.

Assessment.content: Recurrent transient neurological episodes with right hand paresthesia, episodic right upper extremity and leg weakness, and transient gait change, with throat sensation and difficulty holding/drinking during episodes, increasing in frequency over 1.5–2 months, currently well.
Assessment.source_text: 1) Recurrent transient neuro episodes—R hand paresthesia, episodic RUE and leg weakness with transient gait change; throat sensation; difficulty holding/drinking during episodes; ↑ frequency over 1.5–2 mo; currently well.

Assessment.content: Concern for transient ischemic attack (TIA) given family history of carotid disease.

Assessment.content: Self-initiated aspirin use without documented indication.
